topicName: Bug Life Cycle & Defect Tracking Best Practices
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Bug Life Cycle & Defect Tracking Best Practices in Manual Testing"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"In manual testing, identifying a bug is only the first step. Understanding the bug life cycle and enforcing defect tracking best practices ensures that issues are resolved efficiently, communication between QA and development is seamless, and product quality remains high."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding the Bug Life Cycle"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The bug life cycle (or defect life cycle) represents the journey of a defect from its discovery to its closure. While specific workflows vary by organization, a standard bug follows a specific sequence of states."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"New: The tester logs a newly discovered defect in the tracking tool (e.g., Jira)."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Assigned: The lead or project manager reviews the bug and assigns it to the appropriate developer."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Open: The developer begins analyzing and working on fixing the defect."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Fixed: The developer applies a code fix and marks the defect as resolved."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Retested: The QA engineer performs verification testing on the fixed build."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Closed: If the fix is verified successfully, the bug is closed permanently."},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Common Alternative Bug States"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Not all bugs make it straight from creation to closure. Several intermediate states help manage edge cases and disagreements."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Rejected: The bug is deemed invalid, not a bug, or out of scope by the development team."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Deferred: The bug is valid, but the fix is postponed to a future release due to low priority or time constraints."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Duplicate: Another tester has already logged the exact same defect."},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Defect Tracking Best Practices"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Writing a clear, reproducible bug report saves time and minimizes back-and-forth communication between QA and developers. Adhere to these industry best practices when logging defects:"},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use Clear and Descriptive Titles: Summarize the issue concisely. Formula: Module Name - Action - Expected vs Actual Result."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Provide Step-by-Step Reproduction Instructions: List explicit actions so the developer can replicate the issue easily."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Attach Visual Evidence: Always include screenshots, screen recordings, or log files to prove the defect exists."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Define Environment Details: Specify browser, device, operating system, and application version where the bug occurred."},{"order":22,"type":"subheading","text":"Example of a Well-Structured Bug Report"},{"order":23,"type":"code","text":"Title: Checkout - User cannot proceed to payment when applying an expired coupon code
Environment: Chrome v114, Windows 11, Staging Environment
Severity: High | Priority: Medium

Steps to Reproduce:
1. Log in to the application with a valid user account.
2. Add any item to the shopping cart.
3. Navigate to the Checkout page.
4. Enter an expired promo code 'EXPIRED10' in the discount field.
5. Click the 'Apply' button.

Expected Result:
An error message should appear stating 'This promo code has expired' and the payment button should remain disabled or handle the state gracefully.

Actual Result:
The page hangs indefinitely, and the console throws a NullPointerException."}]
